summary: Remote-controlled desktop input and AI-agent execution via hardcoded WebSocket relay
details: remote-claude-daemon opens a persistent WebSocket to the hardcoded relay wss://remote-claude-relay.fly.dev and dispatches inbound messages into system-wide input and local AI-agent execution on the operator's host. cli.js wires ws message events into input.js handleInput, which uses @nut-tree-fork/nut-js to drive mouse and keyboard actions, and into an askClaude path that invokes the local Claude CLI with `--continue -p --dangerously-skip-permissions <prompt>`, allowing arbitrary prompts to run agent actions with permission checks bypassed. A separate `type` message writes attacker-supplied text to the system clipboard (pbcopy/clip/xclip) and issues Cmd/Ctrl+V, injecting text into whatever window is focused (shell, editor, browser). Anyone who controls the relay endpoint (the package author, or anyone who compromises the Fly.dev app) can drive the host's desktop, type into any focused application, and run Claude agent commands with elevated permissions. The tool is user-invoked rather than firing on install, but the entire runtime purpose is remote control of the host through a maintainer-hosted relay with no documented authentication of remote input.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
